A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MB-AIL research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original GridWorld experiments and MuJoCo evaluations, including cumulative rewards, interaction counts, and results across random seeds.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F retain the original empirical results and add network-capacity ablations and a model-misspecification experiment.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same adversarial reward learning, likelihood-based model learning, optimistic planning or rollout selection, and SAC policy updates. The practical implementation moves to Appendix E; the new network variants are experimental ablations rather than a replacement method.

E1.justification: The three MuJoCo environments and original GridWorld tasks remain. Appendix F adds a GridWorld condition with deliberately corrupted next-state information in Bellman updates, extending coverage to transition-model misspecification within the existing domain.

E2.justification: The MuJoCo reward comparisons retain BC, GAIL, and OPT-AIL; interaction comparisons retain OPT-AIL. The original GridWorld comparison with BC also remains. Newly cited theoretical works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 6.2 introduces controlled reward-network depth/width and policy-width sweeps, holding the other network fixed. Appendix F introduces randomly selected misspecified states whose next-state targets are overwritten with (0, 0). Existing demonstration counts and original experimental settings remain; these additions do not establish that the original benchmarks were rerun.

E4.justification: Two substantive analysis questions are added: whether reward learning requires less network capacity than policy learning, and how performance responds to violations of model realizability. Table 5 and Figure 4 provide corresponding ablation and robustness evidence. The original reward-space and stochasticity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The original three-seed MuJoCo and five-seed GridWorld reporting remains unchanged. Figure 4 also uses five seeds, and Table 5 uses the existing mean-plus/minus reporting style. No increased run counts, new confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are stated.

E6.justification: Tables 3 and 4 and the original Figure 2 retain their results. New Table 5 reports, for example, 4169.7 ± 48.3 versus 704.9 ± 112.5 when reducing policy width from 1024 to 256 in the ablation. Figure 4 adds declining returns with increasing misspecification. These are additional results under new conditions, not improvements to the original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The principal upper bounds and existing hard-instance derivations remain. Theorem 5.9 becomes Theorem 5.8 with an explicit average-regret formulation, a constant lower-bound floor for K, and an expert-variance comparison. New Appendix B adds the offline reduction and Lemma B.1's variance proof. These refine the existing theory rather than replace its main rates.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same headline contributions: MB-AIL, horizon-free second-order guarantees, near-optimal online interaction complexity with limited demonstrations, and the logarithmic reward-class gap for expert demonstrations. The added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly explains the offline case K = 1, when the interaction lower bound becomes trivial, and the intended relationship between expert and maximum policy variance. The new experiments add interpretations concerning reward-versus-policy capacity and performance degradation under model misspecification.

D1.justification: v3 documents the new architecture controls and transition-corruption procedure and adds a statement that source code is supplied in supplementary materials. Actual code availability cannot be verified from these PDFs. The existing MuJoCo hyperparameters and baseline repository links are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Shani et al. (2022), Chen et al. (2024), and two Moulin et al. (2025) works, discussing on/off-policy guarantees, discounted imitation learning, prior interaction lower bounds, and Q-function versus reward-class complexity. Much of the original reinforcement-learning background moves to Appendix A rather than being removed.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: related-work background, practical implementation, and GridWorld experiments move into appendices; the lower-bound lemma and proof sketch also move out of the main text. The main empirical narrative now prioritizes MuJoCo and network ablations, with additional reproducibility and administrative statements.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the ICLR template with different typography, author layout, recurring headers, and denser page composition. Retained tables are resized or wrapped into text, Algorithm 2 and GridWorld figures move to appendices, and new Table 5 and Figure 4 display the added analyses.

improvement.justification: The capacity and misspecification analyses, broader comparisons, and clearer offline accounting are useful additions. However, new Lemma B.1 claims expert variance of at least τ²/2, while Appendix D.1 bounds total return within [0, τ], implying variance at most τ²/4. This contradiction undermines the added variance-matching proof. The empirical benefits and unresolved theoretical error leave the net effect on paper quality uncertain.
